key_insight: Under matched conditions, the CV quantum neural network outperforms the DV version for wafer-map defect classification, especially for spatially localized defects like Edge-Loc.
engineering_relevance: For semiconductor yield screening, the result suggests structured CV quantum heads may be a better near-term candidate than DV heads for defect-pattern recognition in industrial inspection pipelines.
method: Shared ~4.3M-parameter CNN backbone with interchangeable heads
Compared classical dense, CV-QNN, and DV-QNN heads under the same setup
Scaled quantum head size across 3, 4, and 8 qumodes/qubits
evidence_signal: On WM-811K eight-class wafer maps, the 4-qumode CV head achieved 79.7% ± 1.8% accuracy versus 61.6% ± 1.4% for DV, with CV recall on Edge-Loc at 0.66 ± 0.06 while DV stayed at ≤0.05 across sizes.
watch_item: Both quantum heads remain below the 85.0% classical baseline, and hardware noise or deeper circuits can further erode DV performance.
paper_title: Bridging Quantum Computing Paradigms toward Semiconductor Yield: A Controlled CV-versus-DV Comparison on Wafer-Map Defect Classification
